clue.text: Official proof of qualification given to student finally

parts.note: a diploma is the certificate proving a qualification

indicators.note: finally tells us to take only the closing letter of the word student

explanation.surface: A graduate is handed their certificate at the end of the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Official' looks like an adjective describing the proof, but it is a noun defining the answer: a diplomat is an official of the foreign service.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat is a government representative abroad, an official of the foreign service.

clue.text: In the world of computers, current source of support available at first

parts.note: taken as written
IT, information technology, is the computing world
I is the physics symbol for electric current
an ally is someone you can call on for backing

explanation.surface: A tech-support note: in computing, the power supply should be ready before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean in the beginning, before later developments.

clue.text: Lear performed on unusual set not with this character, surely?

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first group of letters on top of the second
performed suggests the word Lear is reworked as a play is staged, so its letters are shuffled
unusual tells us the letters of set come out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Someone watching King Lear staged on an odd set wonders whether a particular figure can really belong in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performed' shuffles LEAR into LAER and 'unusual' turns SET into TES; 'on' stacks LAER above TES. The definition is playful: this Shakespearean figure appears in Hamlet, so not alongside Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: Laertes is a character from Hamlet, the brother of Ophelia, so he never shares the stage with King Lear.

clue.text: Piled-up treasure simply enthrals me

indicators.note: in a down clue, piled up means the letters are stacked from the bottom, so they read upwards
enthrals means the words treasure simply hold the letters captive inside them

explanation.surface: A hoarder confesses that a heap of riches is all it takes to captivate them.
explanation.walkthrough: The run RESIM sits inside 'treaSURE SIMply'; 'Piled-up' reads it upwards in the grid. The whole clue doubles as the hoarder's own confession.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser is a hoarder who delights in amassing wealth, so a heap of riches is what captivates such a person.

clue.text: Hit record (shortened version)

indicators.note: shortened version means the word is cut short by dropping its final letter

parts.note: to tape something is to record it

explanation.surface: A chart-topping song is released in an edited radio cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit record' reads as a chart success, but 'Hit' is the definition and 'record' gives TAPE, which loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To tap someone is to strike them lightly.

clue.text: I married mate, a horny type

parts.note: a pal is a mate, a friend

explanation.surface: Someone announces they have wed a partner who is rather randy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horny' suggests lust, but here it means having horns, as an antelope does.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope, an animal bearing horns.

clue.text: I drink a large amount in London borough

parts.note: a sling is a cocktail of spirits, as in Singapore sling
a ton means a great quantity, as in tons of money

explanation.surface: A drinker admits to downing plenty while out in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Islington is an inner district of north London with its own council.

clue.text: Artist produces small painting on climbing mountain

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first piece above the second

parts.note: pic is a short word for a picture

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word mountain's letters are read upwards

parts.note: Ossa is a mountain in Greece, known from the myth of piling Pelion on Ossa

explanation.surface: A painter creates a little landscape while scaling a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns the Greek peak upwards (ASSO) in this down entry; 'on' here just stacks one piece above the other, it is no container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism.

clue.text: Narrow piece of wood one used as weapon

parts.note: a lath is a thin strip of wood used in building
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone picks up a thin strip of timber and swings it like a club.
explanation.walkthrough: A lathi is a heavy bamboo stick used as a weapon, especially by police in South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathi is a long iron-bound stick wielded as a club in India.

clue.text: Revolting ex-con banished by community

indicators.note: banished by means the ex-con is thrown out of the community, removing those letters

parts.note: a village is a small rural community
an old lag is a former convict, so lag stands for one

explanation.surface: Locals drive out a released prisoner whose conduct disgusted them.
explanation.walkthrough: LAG is British slang for a convict, usually an 'old lag'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean disgusting or repulsive.

clue.text: Ask for drink and dish with lots of ice in

parts.note: to sup is to drink in sips

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the dish

parts.note: a plate is a dish

indicators.note: lots of means most but not all of the word ice is used, dropping its last letter

explanation.surface: A customer orders a beverage and a plate of something heaped with ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots of' means most of the ice, so it loses its final letter (IC); 'in' sends that into the dish. 'Ask for' is the definition, not a request for the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To supplicate is to beg or plead humbly for something.

clue.text: Monk retiring so certain to be refreshed

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the letters of the Latin word run backwards

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus, used to mark a quotation as printed

indicators.note: refreshed means made new again, so the letters of certain are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman going to bed is sure of waking rested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns SIC into CIS; 'to be refreshed' rearranges CERTAIN into TERCIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cistercians are a strict order of monks founded at Citeaux in France.

clue.text: Piece of land in island like this stretches over miles

indicators.note: stretches over means the phrase like this extends around the miles

parts.note: thus means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: A geographer describes a strip of ground on an island running for miles in this shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretches over' has 'like this' spread around the miles. 'island' gives its short form, as on maps.
explanation.definitionFit: An isthmus is a narrow strip of ground joining two larger landmasses.

clue.text: Prison riot

explanation.definitionFit: In slang a stir is a jail, and a stir is also a commotion or uproar.

clue.text: Veteran soldier's nervous state, leaving the front

indicators.note: leaving the front means the first letter departs from the phrase, like a soldier quitting the front line

parts.note: a cold sweat is a state of fear or anxiety

explanation.surface: An old campaigner suffers anxiety after returning from the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the front' looks like the battle line, but it means the first letter of COLD SWEAT. OLD SWEAT is British slang for a long-serving soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sweat is an experienced, long-serving soldier, a hardened veteran.

clue.text: Old scoundrels I encountered on trip

parts.note: ex means former, old
curs are contemptible men, scoundrels
to happen on something is to encounter it

explanation.surface: Someone recalls bumping into some old rogues while travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: An excursion is a short outing or journey made for pleasure.

clue.text: Husband, a most eccentric fellow

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or odd, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wife describes her partner as a thoroughly odd character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges H plus A MOST into the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas is a man's name, standing for any male person.

clue.text: Everyone present collars me for change

indicators.note: for change means the letters of collars me are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A man is grabbed by the collar and told to swap his outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for change' rearranges COLLARS ME.
explanation.definitionFit: All-comers means anyone who turns up, every person who arrives.

clue.text: Government official reported offence to detective

indicators.note: reported means the phrase is spoken, so we want letters that sound like it

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing, an offence; dick is slang for a detective, as in private dick

explanation.surface: A civil servant passes on a crime report to an investigator.
explanation.walkthrough: SIN DICK said out loud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndic is a magistrate or representative appointed to manage a city's or body's affairs.

clue.text: Doctor being diligent to begin with put bandage on

parts.note: esse is Latin for to be, meaning being or existence

indicators.note: to begin with means only the first letter of diligent is taken

explanation.surface: A conscientious physician starts treatment by binding the wound.
explanation.walkthrough: ESSE is Latin for 'being', as in 'in esse'.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress a wound is to apply a bandage to it.

clue.text: I pop into factory, one preventing kiddies from coming along

definitions.text: one preventing kiddies from coming along

indicators.note: into means the short pieces go inside the factory

parts.note: a mill is a factory, as in a cotton mill
to nip in is to pop in, make a quick visit

explanation.surface: Someone drops in on a factory, apparently one that puts a stop to children arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: To nip into a shop is to pop into it; 'into' sends that and I inside the factory. The definition is a playful description of the contraceptive.
explanation.definitionFit: The minipill is a progestogen-only contraceptive pill, which prevents pregnancy.

clue.text: Drug addict's articles locked away by school

indicators.note: locked away by means the articles are shut inside the school

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
the is the definite article
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A user's belongings are confiscated by the school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a group of whales, a POD, not a place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A pothead is slang for a habitual cannabis user.

clue.text: Primate burying saint in part of church

indicators.note: burying means the saint is placed inside the primate

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: An ape inters a holy man in a corner of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' looks like an archbishop, which suits a church, but here it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is the vaulted recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Walk round, making a video

parts.note: a prom, short for promenade, is a walk along the seafront
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A stroll round town becomes a filmed clip.
explanation.definitionFit: A promo is a short promotional film, especially one made for a pop single.

clue.text: Note problem and point out fresh start is needed

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a sum is an arithmetic problem

indicators.note: out means the letters of point are put out of order

explanation.surface: A teacher spots a problem and says it must be begun again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges POINT into PTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A resumption is the restarting of something after a pause.

clue.text: Test given after start of maths lesson

indicators.note: given after places the test below the opening letter in this down clue
start of means only the first letter of maths is taken

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A spoken exam follows the opening of a maths class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lesson' looks like a class, but here it is the moral of a story.
explanation.definitionFit: The moral of a story is the lesson it teaches.

clue.text: What's eaten by terriers in mess?

definitions.meaning: the meal a dog is given

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally it is a dog's meal; idiomatically a dog's dinner is a shambles.

clue.text: Equine plague

definitions.meaning: a horse, especially an old or worn-out one

explanation.definitionFit: A nag is an old horse, and to nag is to harass someone with constant complaints.

clue.text: Watches front part of ship

definitions.meaning: the ... of a ship are the very front of the bow, where hawse holes once were painted with ...

explanation.definitionFit: To eye is to watch, and the eyes are a nautical term for the forward part of the bows.

clue.text: Fruit tree with string attached

parts.note: a cord is a length of string
on means attached, as in a lid that is on

explanation.surface: A gardener ties an orchard tree with twine.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordon is a fruit tree pruned and trained to grow as a single stem.

clue.text: Ageing lady's wearing medal, award for record sales

indicators.note: wearing means the medal wraps around the old lady as clothing does

parts.note: GC is the George Cross, a British gallantry medal
old means ageing
Di is a woman's name, so lady's gives Di's

explanation.surface: An elderly woman pins on a decoration recognising her huge record sales.
explanation.walkthrough: The George Cross is a British medal for bravery; 'wearing' has the medal go round the old lady, as clothing wraps a body. Di is a stock crossword woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold disc is presented to an artist when a record sells a set number of copies.
